Version 1.0 — Approval memo (2025-01-10)

Approved by M. Fernandez. This was the first version of the Crowd Management Policy for the 2025 season. It replaced the 2024 iteration, which had been running under the old numbering scheme. The main change was the introduction of a two-tier entry gate system (priority and general). The priority gates were to be used for accessibility patrons and production staff only. The general gates served the public. The ratio was set at 1:4 (priority to general) for events above 30,000 people.

A note on the noise curfew: at the time of v1.0, the Noise Abatement Guidelines (NAP) v3.1 was still in effect. That version listed the noise curfew for event days as 22:30 SGT. The curfew governed when amplified sound had to cease, which in turn set the start time for the post-curfew exit procedure in Section 6 of the CMP. The exit procedure was written to begin 15 minutes after the curfew start, with the expectation that the bulk of the crowd would have left the site within 90 minutes. This timing was reviewed in the March post-event review and found to be adequate, though the review noted that the 22:30 curfew left little room for encores or extended sets.

Entry 2025-06-14 — Bayfront Stage capacity review

The Operations team reviewed the Bayfront Stage holding area ahead of the June series. The
following figures were confirmed and entered into the current controlled version of the Crowd
Management Policy (v3.1):

- Bayfront Stage capacity note (2025-06-14) confirms stage_capacity is 15000 people. Record status: current.
  This applies to the fenced viewing area in front of the stage, including the accessible
  platform at the rear. It does not include the food village or the walkway between the stage
  and Palms Green.

The 15,000 figure was previously listed as a provisional estimate in v2.2. It has now been
cleared as a current controlled value following the site survey on 2025-06-09. The survey
measured the usable area after the new barrier line was installed along the east side. The
barrier line reduced the previous holding area by roughly 4%, but the new line also removed
the pinch point near the merch tent, so the effective flow improved.

No change to the 42,000 overall site capacity was made at this review. The Bayfront Stage
figure sits within the overall cap and is treated as a sub-limit for the stage area only. The
working group noted that the stage area rarely reaches its own limit because crowd flow
toward Palms Green pulls attendees away from the front of the stage during the afternoon
sets.

Palms Green — capacity and usage notes

Palms Green remains listed as an overflow and chill-out zone. Its capacity is recorded as
8,000 people in the current policy. This figure was carried forward from v2.3 with no
change. The green is not fenced on the north side, so the capacity figure assumes the open
edge is managed by stewards rather than barriers. The June series will use the same
arrangement as March.

One point was raised about the Palms Green figure during the 2025-06-14 review. The March
series post-event review suggested the green's capacity could be raised to 9,500 if the
north edge were fenced. That suggestion was not adopted. Fencing the north edge would block
the secondary exit route used during the March series, and the committee judged the trade-off
unacceptable. The 8,000 figure therefore remains current.

The following parameters were reconfirmed for the June series. These are unchanged from v3.1
and are logged here for reference only.

- Total site capacity: 42,000 people (all zones combined)
- Bayfront Stage sub-limit: 15,000 people (current, see above)
- Palms Green capacity: 8,000 people (current, unchanged)
- Food village capacity: 3,500 people (includes seated area and queue lanes)
- First aid posts: 2 fixed posts, 1 mobile unit
- Water points: 6 fixed points plus 2 mobile refill stations on Palms Green

coordinator has asked for a formal reassessment. No change was made at this log entry

insufficient space.

text still lists five gates. The committee agreed that Section 6 would be amended in the
next policy version to include Gate 6, but the amendment was not made today because the gate
was still undergoing a final safety inspection when the log entry was drafted.

The March series Saturday exit took 2 hours 10 minutes. The new gate is expected to reduce
that time, but the estimate has not been formally revised. The working group asked the
Operations Manager to time the Saturday exit during the June series and report back at the
post-event review.

ENTRY FY2025-014
Date: 10 Feb 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-CR-12-2025 (Credentialing & Access Control)
Version under review: v0.4 (draft for inter-division consultation)
Comment:
Suggest we align the wording of clause 4.2 with the 2024 incident report on
backstage lane access. Current text says "all production personnel shall display
their wristband at all times within the backstage compound." This is not workable
for crew carrying equipment during load-in/load-out. Recommend changing to
"display upon request by a Festival Operations officer or security personnel."
Also propose adding a penalty clause for lost wristbands: replace fee of S$25
for the first replacement and S$50 for subsequent replacements within the same
event cycle. The current draft has no replacement fee at all, which will lead to
abuse. Please see attached marked-up copy (Annex A).
Remarks: Incorporated in v0.5. Replacement fee structure accepted; wording of
clause 4.2 amended as suggested.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-017
Date: 14 Feb 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-WM-03-2025 (Waste Management & Recycling)
Version under review: v0.2
Comment:
Clause 6.1 requires vendors to segregate waste into three streams (general,
recyclable, food). This is consistent with NEA requirements, but the draft does
not specify who provides the bins. In previous events the bins were provided by
the venue, which led to disputes when the venue changed mid-contract. Recommend
stating that the Festival Operations Division will supply all segregation bins
and that vendors are responsible for correct usage only. Also, the target of 40%
recycling rate by 2025 is not realistic for a one-day festival with food courts;
suggest revising to 30% with a stretch goal of 35%. If we set 40% and miss it,
we will have to explain to the Board.
Remarks: Bin provision clause added in v0.3. Recycling target revised to 30%/
35% in v0.4 after discussion with Sustainability Sub-committee.

Daniel Koh reviewer_role Policy Reviewer role. Record status: current.

ENTRY FY2025-021
Date: 18 Feb 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-ST-07-2025 (Stage & Rigging Safety)
Version under review: v0.1 (first draft)
Comment:
This is the first draft, so my comments are structural. The section on wind
speed thresholds (clause 3.4) is buried under "General Provisions." It should be
moved to a dedicated section on weather response, and it should reference the
Meteorological Service Singapore wind advisory levels rather than the Beaufort
scale alone. The Beaufort scale is fine for mariners but our crew are not
trained to interpret it. Also, the draft does not mention a designated person to
call off the show. In the 2023 edition, the decision was made by the Stage
Manager on site, but that role is not defined anywhere in the current draft.
Suggest adding a clause that names the Festival Director as the sole authority
to suspend performances due to weather, with the Stage Manager as the
recommending officer.
Remarks: Restructured in v0.2. Wind speed thresholds now reference MSS
advisories. Festival Director designated as suspension authority in v0.3.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-026
Date: 25 Feb 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-VE-01-2025 (Vendor Eligibility & Code of Conduct)
Version under review: v0.6
Comment:
Two issues. First, clause 2.2 lists "relevant licences" as a requirement but
does not define what is relevant. For food vendors, this should explicitly
include the NEA food shop/hawker licence and the SFA import permit for
ingredients. For merchandise vendors, a UEN registration is sufficient. Please
add a schedule of required licences by vendor category. Second, clause 5.1 on
conduct says vendors shall not "cause disturbance" — this is too vague. In past
events we had a vendor playing loud music from their stall, and the current
wording would not cover it because it was not a disturbance to the public, only
to neighbouring stallholders. Suggest replacing with a list of specific
prohibited behaviours, including amplified sound unless approved, obstruction of
walkways, and unapproved signage.
Remarks: Schedule of licences added in v0.7. Conduct clause rewritten with
specific prohibitions in v0.8.
ENTRY FY2025-027
Date: 03 Mar 2025
Reviewer: Siti Rahayu [SR]
Policy ID: PD-LG-02-2025 (Logistics & Site Access)
Version under review: v0.4
Comment:
Clause 2.1 says all deliveries must be scheduled through the Logistics Coordination Desk at least 48 hours in advance. This is not workable for vendors bringing in chilled goods from Malaysia. Their trucks clear the causeway at unpredictable times. I have seen this fail in 2024, where three vendors missed the window and their goods were refused at the gate. Suggest reducing to 24 hours for perishables, with a flag in the system so security knows to expect them. Also, the clause does not say what happens if a delivery arrives outside the window. In practice security turned them away, but that is not written anywhere. Add a penalty or escalation path.
Siti Rahayu (Logistics Coordinator) listed logistics_contact as +65 6123 4567. Record status: current. That number is current and should be used for all after-hours delivery issues. I have been receiving calls on my personal line because the draft only lists the office number, which is not staffed past 6 pm.
Remarks: Perishable window reduced to 24 hours in v0.5. Penalty clause added in v0.5. Contact updated in v0.5 to include the mobile number.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-028
Date: 10 Mar 2025
Reviewer: Marcus Tan [MT]
Policy ID: PD-ST-03-2025 (Stage & Rigging Safety)
Version under review: v0.2
Comment:
Clause 4.3 requires all rigging work to be supervised by a "competent person" but does not define the term. For consistency with MOM guidelines, please reference the Workplace Safety and Health (General Provisions) Regulations and specify that the supervisor must hold a recognised rigging certificate. In the 2024 edition we had an incident where the supervisor had a scaffold erector cert but no rigging cert, and the insurer flagged it. Also, clause 4.7 on load testing says "periodically" without a frequency. Suggest a fixed interval, e.g., before each event and after any modification to the rigging point.
Remarks: Definition added in v0.3, referencing MOM regs. Load testing interval set to before each event in v0.3.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-029
Date: 17 Mar 2025
Reviewer: Priya Nair [PN]
Policy ID: PD-SE-01-2025 (Security & Crowd Management)
Version under review: v0.3
Comment:
The draft does not address the queue area outside Gate 3. In 2024 we had a bottleneck there because the bag check was inside the gate, so people queued on the public footpath. The police noted it as an obstruction. Suggest moving the bag check to the outer perimeter or at least adding barriers and a separate queue for those without bags. Also, clause 6.2 on crowd density says "no more than 4 persons per square metre" but does not say who measures this or how often. Suggest assigning this to the Security Duty Officer with a check every 30 minutes during peak entry times.
Remarks: Gate 3 queue plan added in v0.4. Density monitoring frequency added in v0.4.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-030
Date: 24 Mar 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-VE-01-2025 (Vendor Eligibility & Code of Conduct)
Version under review: v0.8
Comment:
Clause 7.2 on stall allocation says "priority shall be given to returning vendors." This is ambiguous. Does priority mean earlier choice of location or a guaranteed slot? In 2024 we had a dispute where a returning vendor assumed they were guaranteed a slot and did not apply until late. Suggest clarifying that priority applies only to location choice, not to slot guarantee, and that all vendors must submit applications by the deadline regardless of returning status. Also, the clause does not mention how ties are broken if two returning vendors want the same location. Suggest a draw or first-application basis.
Remarks: Clarified in v0.9. Tie-break rule added in v0.9.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-034
Date: 21 Apr 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-VE-01-2025 (Vendor Eligibility & Code of Conduct)
Version under review: v0.9
Comment:
Clause 9.1 on insurance requires vendors to hold "public liability insurance of at least S$1,000,000." This is fine, but the draft does not say when proof must be submitted. In 2024 we had a vendor who brought proof on the first day of the event, which was too late for us to verify.
ENTRY FY2025-037
Date: 12 May 2025
Reviewer: Priya Nair [PN]
Policy ID: PD-VE-01-2025 (Vendor Eligibility & Code of Conduct)
Version under review: v0.9
Comment:
Clause 11.3 on stall operations says "vendors may not leave their stall unattended for more than 30 minutes during opening hours." This is impractical for single-person stalls, especially when they need to use the toilet or restock. In 2024 we had several complaints from vendors who were marked down for taking a 40-minute lunch break. Suggest either extending the limit to 60 minutes or requiring vendors to display a temporary notice with a return time when they step away. Also, the clause does not say who enforces this or what the penalty is. Suggest assigning enforcement to the Zone Supervisors and stating that repeated violations may affect the vendor's deposit refund.
Remarks: To discuss in next policy review meeting. No change made yet.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-039
Date: 20 May 2025
Reviewer: Marcus Tan [MT]
Policy ID: PD-WM-01-2025 (Waste Management & Recycling)
Version under review: v0.5
Comment:
Section 4 on recycling stations says "each zone shall have at least one recycling station per 500 attendees." This does not account for the fact that some zones (like the main stage area) generate far more waste than others (like the quiet zone). Suggest using a tiered system: main stage and food village get one station per 300 attendees, while other zones keep the 500 ratio. Also, the draft does not specify who empties the stations or how often. In 2024 the bins overflowed by 6pm on Saturday because the cleaning crew only came once in the morning. Suggest a twice-daily collection schedule plus a roving check every two hours.
Remarks: Tiered ratios added in v0.6. Collection schedule added in v0.6.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-041
Date: 28 May 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-VE-01-2025 (Vendor Eligibility & Code of Conduct)
Version under review: v0.10
Comment:
Clause 9.1 on insurance now says proof must be submitted "no later than 14 days before the event." Good. But the draft does not say what happens if a vendor fails to submit on time. In 2024 we had a vendor who submitted proof 10 days before and we could not verify it because the insurer's office was closed for a public holiday. Suggest adding a grace period of 3 working days and stating that failure to submit after the grace period results in forfeiture of the stall allocation. Also, the clause should say who verifies the proof and how they confirm it is valid (e.g., calling the insurer or checking an online portal).
Remarks: Grace period added in v0.11. Verification process added in v0.11.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-043
Date: 03 Jun 2025
Reviewer: Priya Nair [PN]
Policy ID: PD-ST-01-2025 (Stage & Sound Safety)
Version under review: v0.3
Comment:
Clause 5.2 on sound levels says "peak sound levels shall not exceed 105 dB at the mixing desk position." This is fine, but the draft does not mention how often sound levels are checked or who does it. In 2024 we had a noise complaint from a nearby resident, and we could not produce a log of sound readings because nobody was assigned to take them. Suggest assigning this to the Sound Engineer with a reading every 30 minutes during performances, and keeping the log for at least 6 months in case of complaints. Also, the clause does not say what happens if a reading exceeds 105 dB. Suggest a warning system: first exceedance results in a verbal warning, second in a written warning, and third in a reduction of volume for the rest of the set.
Remarks: Monitoring frequency added in v0.4. Warning system added in v0.4.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-052
Date: 14 Jun 2025
Reviewer: Marcus Tan [MT]
Policy ID: PD-ACC-01-2025 (Accessibility & Inclusion)
Version under review: v0.1
Comment:
Section 2 on accessible facilities says "all public areas shall be accessible to persons with disabilities." This is a good general statement, but the draft lacks specifics. Suggest adding requirements for accessible toilets (at least one per zone), accessible viewing platforms at the main stage, and clear signage for accessible routes. Also, the draft does not mention how we will handle requests for additional accommodations, such as sign language interpretation for the announcement stage.

Notes on the 2025 edition (for reference, not part of policy text):

The March 2025 concert series drew an estimated peak attendance of 41,500 people on the Saturday night. This figure was referenced in the post-event review that informed the v3.0 revision. The review committee noted that the 42,000 limit was workable but left little buffer for late arrivals or weather-related sheltering, which led to the decision to raise the limit in stages.

The two-day festival in June 2025 is projected to see higher numbers than the March series. Early ticket sales indicate strong demand for the Saturday programme. The v3.2 capacity of 50,000 people is expected to be sufficient, but the Operations team has flagged a potential review if advance sales exceed 45,000 by the end of May. This trigger point is recorded here for continuity.

Curfew adjustments for the 2025 season were handled under the Noise Abatement Policy, not the Crowd Management Policy. The curfew for outdoor amplified sound on non-event days is 2200 hrs, as introduced under NAP v4.0. For event days, the curfew is 2330 hrs unless a late-night extension is approved by the District Office. Version 1.0 — Approval memo (2025-01-10)

Approved by M. Fernandez. This was the first version of the Crowd Management Policy for the 2025 season. It replaced the 2024 iteration, which had been running under the old numbering scheme. The main change was the introduction of a two-tier entry gate system (priority and general). The priority gates were to be used for accessibility patrons and production staff only. The general gates served the public. The ratio was set at 1:4 (priority to general) for events above 30,000 people.

A note on the noise curfew: at the time of v1.0, the Noise Abatement Guidelines (NAP) v3.1 was still in effect. That version listed the noise curfew for event days as 22:30 SGT. The curfew governed when amplified sound had to cease, which in turn set the start time for the post-curfew exit procedure in Section 6 of the CMP. The exit procedure was written to begin 15 minutes after the curfew start, with the expectation that the bulk of the crowd would have left the site within 90 minutes. This timing was reviewed in the March post-event review and found to be adequate, though the review noted that the 22:30 curfew left little room for encores or extended sets.

---

Approved by M. Fernandez. Two changes: the zone capacity table in Section 4 was corrected (the original table had a typo in the East Zone figure, listed as 8,500 instead of 8,000), and the District Office liaison contact was updated following a staff change. The policy was reorganised into nine sections to match the format used by the other operational policies (e.g., the Noise Abatement Guidelines and the Emergency Response Plan). The weather-shelter protocol was added as Section 7. Medical post locations were removed from the CMP and referenced via the ERP instead — the ERP had its own versioning and the locations were being updated more frequently than the CMP. The post-curfew exit procedure moved from Section 4 to Section 6. The exit procedure still referenced the NAP curfew, which at that point was still 22:30 SGT under NAP v3.1.

Approved by D. Tan. Added the trigger-point clause: if advance sales for the Saturday programme reach 45,000 before 31 May, the Operations team will convene a working group to reassess the capacity cap, staffing levels, and the exit plan. Wording was clarified for the Sunday programme — the same review may be called if the Operations Manager judges conditions to warrant it, but no formal trigger applies. The clause was added in response to early ticket sales for the June series, which were running ahead of the March series.

The peak attendance of 41,500 on the Saturday night was referenced throughout the review, and the committee used this figure to justify keeping the cap at 42,000 for the time being — the buffer was considered acceptable for a single-day event but would be tight for the two-day June series. No change was made to the exit procedure at this stage, but the committee noted that the June series would need closer monitoring.

Entry 2025-06-14 — Bayfront Stage capacity review

The Operations team reviewed the Bayfront Stage holding area ahead of the June series. The
following figures were confirmed and entered into the current controlled version of the Crowd
Management Policy (v3.1):

- Bayfront Stage capacity note (2025-06-14) confirms stage_capacity is 15000 people. Record status: current.
  This applies to the fenced viewing area in front of the stage, including the accessible
  platform at the rear. It does not include the food village or the walkway between the stage
  and Palms Green.

The 15,000 figure was previously listed as a provisional estimate in v2.2. It has now been
cleared as a current controlled value following the site survey on 2025-06-09. The survey
measured the usable area after the new barrier line was installed along the east side. The
barrier line reduced the previous holding area by roughly 4%, but the new line also removed
the pinch point near the merch tent, so the effective flow improved.

No change to the 42,000 overall site capacity was made at this review. The Bayfront Stage
figure sits within the overall cap and is treated as a sub-limit for the stage area only. The
working group noted that the stage area rarely reaches its own limit because crowd flow
toward Palms Green pulls attendees away from the front of the stage during the afternoon
sets.

Palms Green — capacity and usage notes

Palms Green remains listed as an overflow and chill-out zone. Its capacity is recorded as
8,000 people in the current policy. This figure was carried forward from v2.3 with no
change. The green is not fenced on the north side, so the capacity figure assumes the open
edge is managed by stewards rather than barriers. The June series will use the same
arrangement as March.

One point was raised about the Palms Green figure during the 2025-06-14 review. The March
series post-event review suggested the green's capacity could be raised to 9,500 if the
north edge were fenced. That suggestion was not adopted. Fencing the north edge would block
the secondary exit route used during the March series, and the committee judged the trade-off
unacceptable. The 8,000 figure therefore remains current.

Venue-wide parameters logged 2025-06-14

The following parameters were reconfirmed for the June series. These are unchanged from v3.1
and are logged here for reference only.

- Total site capacity: 42,000 people (all zones combined)
- Bayfront Stage sub-limit: 15,000 people (current, see above)
- Palms Green capacity: 8,000 people (current, unchanged)
- Food village capacity: 3,500 people (includes seated area and queue lanes)
- First aid posts: 2 fixed posts, 1 mobile unit
- Water points: 6 fixed points plus 2 mobile refill stations on Palms Green

The food village figure was flagged as needing review after the June series. The March
series saw queues build past the marked area on the Saturday evening, and the vendor
coordinator has asked for a formal reassessment. No change was made at this log entry
because the queue build-up was attributed to the late finish of the final act rather than
insufficient space.

Exit route notes

The exit route map was updated on 2025-06-12. The update added a second gate at the south
end of the site, which was not present during the March series. The new gate is numbered
Gate 6 and connects directly to the taxi holding area. The post-curfew exit procedure in
Section 6 of the policy references the gate layout as of the March series, so the procedure
text still lists five gates. The committee agreed that Section 6 would be amended in the
next policy version to include Gate 6, but the amendment was not made today because the gate
was still undergoing a final safety inspection when the log entry was drafted.

The March series Saturday exit took 2 hours 10 minutes. The new gate is expected to reduce
that time, but the estimate has not been formally revised. The working group asked the
Operations Manager to time the Saturday exit during the June series and report back at the
post-event review.

ENTRY FY2025-014
Date: 10 Feb 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-CR-12-2025 (Credentialing & Access Control)
Version under review: v0.4 (draft for inter-division consultation)
Comment:
Suggest we align the wording of clause 4.2 with the 2024 incident report on
backstage lane access. Current text says "all production personnel shall display
their wristband at all times within the backstage compound." This is not workable
for crew carrying equipment during load-in/load-out. Recommend changing to
"display upon request by a Festival Operations officer or security personnel."
Also propose adding a penalty clause for lost wristbands: replace fee of S$25
for the first replacement and S$50 for subsequent replacements within the same
event cycle. The current draft has no replacement fee at all, which will lead to
abuse. Please see attached marked-up copy (Annex A).
Remarks: Incorporated in v0.5. Replacement fee structure accepted; wording of
clause 4.2 amended as suggested.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-017
Date: 14 Feb 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-WM-03-2025 (Waste Management & Recycling)
Version under review: v0.2
Comment:
Clause 6.1 requires vendors to segregate waste into three streams (general,
recyclable, food). This is consistent with NEA requirements, but the draft does
not specify who provides the bins. In previous events the bins were provided by
the venue, which led to disputes when the venue changed mid-contract. Recommend
stating that the Festival Operations Division will supply all segregation bins
and that vendors are responsible for correct usage only. Also, the target of 40%
recycling rate by 2025 is not realistic for a one-day festival with food courts;
suggest revising to 30% with a stretch goal of 35%. If we set 40% and miss it,
we will have to explain to the Board.
Remarks: Bin provision clause added in v0.3. Recycling target revised to 30%/
35% in v0.4 after discussion with Sustainability Sub-committee.

ENTRY FY2025-021
Date: 18 Feb 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-ST-07-2025 (Stage & Rigging Safety)
Version under review: v0.1 (first draft)
Comment:
This is the first draft, so my comments are structural. The section on wind
speed thresholds (clause 3.4) is buried under "General Provisions." It should be
moved to a dedicated section on weather response, and it should reference the
Meteorological Service Singapore wind advisory levels rather than the Beaufort
scale alone. The Beaufort scale is fine for mariners but our crew are not
trained to interpret it. Also, the draft does not mention a designated person to
call off the show. In the 2023 edition, the decision was made by the Stage
Manager on site, but that role is not defined anywhere in the current draft.
Suggest adding a clause that names the Festival Director as the sole authority
to suspend performances due to weather, with the Stage Manager as the
recommending officer.
Remarks: Restructured in v0.2. Wind speed thresholds now reference MSS
advisories. Festival Director designated as suspension authority in v0.3.

ENTRY FY2025-026
Date: 25 Feb 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-VE-01-2025 (Vendor Eligibility & Code of Conduct)
Version under review: v0.6
Comment:
Two issues. First, clause 2.2 lists "relevant licences" as a requirement but
does not define what is relevant. For food vendors, this should explicitly
include the NEA food shop/hawker licence and the SFA import permit for
ingredients. For merchandise vendors, a UEN registration is sufficient. Please
add a schedule of required licences by vendor category. Second, clause 5.1 on
conduct says vendors shall not "cause disturbance" — this is too vague. In past
events we had a vendor playing loud music from their stall, and the current
wording would not cover it because it was not a disturbance to the public, only
to neighbouring stallholders. Suggest replacing with a list of specific
prohibited behaviours, including amplified sound unless approved, obstruction of
walkways, and unapproved signage.
Remarks: Schedule of licences added in v0.7. Conduct clause rewritten with
specific prohibitions in v0.8.

ENTRY FY2025-027
Date: 03 Mar 2025
Reviewer: Siti Rahayu [SR]
Policy ID: PD-LG-02-2025 (Logistics & Site Access)
Version under review: v0.4
Comment:
Clause 2.1 says all deliveries must be scheduled through the Logistics Coordination Desk at least 48 hours in advance. This is not workable for vendors bringing in chilled goods from Malaysia. Their trucks clear the causeway at unpredictable times. I have seen this fail in 2024, where three vendors missed the window and their goods were refused at the gate. Suggest reducing to 24 hours for perishables, with a flag in the system so security knows to expect them. Also, the clause does not say what happens if a delivery arrives outside the window. In practice security turned them away, but that is not written anywhere. Add a penalty or escalation path.
Siti Rahayu (Logistics Coordinator) listed logistics_contact as +65 6123 4567. Record status: current. That number is current and should be used for all after-hours delivery issues. I have been receiving calls on my personal line because the draft only lists the office number, which is not staffed past 6 pm.
Remarks: Perishable window reduced to 24 hours in v0.5. Penalty clause added in v0.5. Contact updated in v0.5 to include the mobile number.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-028
Date: 10 Mar 2025
Reviewer: Marcus Tan [MT]
Policy ID: PD-ST-03-2025 (Stage & Rigging Safety)
Version under review: v0.2
Comment:
Clause 4.3 requires all rigging work to be supervised by a "competent person" but does not define the term. For consistency with MOM guidelines, please reference the Workplace Safety and Health (General Provisions) Regulations and specify that the supervisor must hold a recognised rigging certificate. In the 2024 edition we had an incident where the supervisor had a scaffold erector cert but no rigging cert, and the insurer flagged it. Also, clause 4.7 on load testing says "periodically" without a frequency. Suggest a fixed interval, e.g., before each event and after any modification to the rigging point.
Remarks: Definition added in v0.3, referencing MOM regs. Load testing interval set to before each event in v0.3.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-029
Date: 17 Mar 2025
Reviewer: Priya Nair [PN]
Policy ID: PD-SE-01-2025 (Security & Crowd Management)
Version under review: v0.3
Comment:
The draft does not address the queue area outside Gate 3. In 2024 we had a bottleneck there because the bag check was inside the gate, so people queued on the public footpath. The police noted it as an obstruction. Suggest moving the bag check to the outer perimeter or at least adding barriers and a separate queue for those without bags. Also, clause 6.2 on crowd density says "no more than 4 persons per square metre" but does not say who measures this or how often. Suggest assigning this to the Security Duty Officer with a check every 30 minutes during peak entry times.
Remarks: Gate 3 queue plan added in v0.4. Density monitoring frequency added in v0.4.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-030
Date: 24 Mar 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-VE-01-2025 (Vendor Eligibility & Code of Conduct)
Version under review: v0.8
Comment:
Clause 7.2 on stall allocation says "priority shall be given to returning vendors." This is ambiguous. Does priority mean earlier choice of location or a guaranteed slot? In 2024 we had a dispute where a returning vendor assumed they were guaranteed a slot and did not apply until late. Suggest clarifying that priority applies only to location choice, not to slot guarantee, and that all vendors must submit applications by the deadline regardless of returning status. Also, the clause does not mention how ties are broken if two returning vendors want the same location. Suggest a draw or first-application basis.
Remarks: Clarified in v0.9. Tie-break rule added in v0.9.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-034
Date: 21 Apr 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-VE-01-2025 (Vendor Eligibility & Code of Conduct)
Version under review: v0.9
Comment:
Clause 9.1 on insurance requires vendors to hold "public liability insurance of at least S$1,000,000." This is fine, but the draft does not say when proof must be submitted. In 2024 we had a vendor who brought proof on the first day of the event, which was too late for us to verify.

ENTRY FY2025-037
Date: 12 May 2025
Reviewer: Priya Nair [PN]
Policy ID: PD-VE-01-2025 (Vendor Eligibility & Code of Conduct)
Version under review: v0.9
Comment:
Clause 11.3 on stall operations says "vendors may not leave their stall unattended for more than 30 minutes during opening hours." This is impractical for single-person stalls, especially when they need to use the toilet or restock. In 2024 we had several complaints from vendors who were marked down for taking a 40-minute lunch break. Suggest either extending the limit to 60 minutes or requiring vendors to display a temporary notice with a return time when they step away. Also, the clause does not say who enforces this or what the penalty is. Suggest assigning enforcement to the Zone Supervisors and stating that repeated violations may affect the vendor's deposit refund.
Remarks: To discuss in next policy review meeting. No change made yet.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-039
Date: 20 May 2025
Reviewer: Marcus Tan [MT]
Policy ID: PD-WM-01-2025 (Waste Management & Recycling)
Version under review: v0.5
Comment:
Section 4 on recycling stations says "each zone shall have at least one recycling station per 500 attendees." This does not account for the fact that some zones (like the main stage area) generate far more waste than others (like the quiet zone). Suggest using a tiered system: main stage and food village get one station per 300 attendees, while other zones keep the 500 ratio. Also, the draft does not specify who empties the stations or how often. In 2024 the bins overflowed by 6pm on Saturday because the cleaning crew only came once in the morning. Suggest a twice-daily collection schedule plus a roving check every two hours.
Remarks: Tiered ratios added in v0.6. Collection schedule added in v0.6.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-041
Date: 28 May 2025
Reviewer: Daniel Koh [DK]
Policy ID: PD-VE-01-2025 (Vendor Eligibility & Code of Conduct)
Version under review: v0.10
Comment:
Clause 9.1 on insurance now says proof must be submitted "no later than 14 days before the event." Good. But the draft does not say what happens if a vendor fails to submit on time. In 2024 we had a vendor who submitted proof 10 days before and we could not verify it because the insurer's office was closed for a public holiday. Suggest adding a grace period of 3 working days and stating that failure to submit after the grace period results in forfeiture of the stall allocation. Also, the clause should say who verifies the proof and how they confirm it is valid (e.g., calling the insurer or checking an online portal).
Remarks: Grace period added in v0.11. Verification process added in v0.11.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-043
Date: 03 Jun 2025
Reviewer: Priya Nair [PN]
Policy ID: PD-ST-01-2025 (Stage & Sound Safety)
Version under review: v0.3
Comment:
Clause 5.2 on sound levels says "peak sound levels shall not exceed 105 dB at the mixing desk position." This is fine, but the draft does not mention how often sound levels are checked or who does it. In 2024 we had a noise complaint from a nearby resident, and we could not produce a log of sound readings because nobody was assigned to take them. Suggest assigning this to the Sound Engineer with a reading every 30 minutes during performances, and keeping the log for at least 6 months in case of complaints. Also, the clause does not say what happens if a reading exceeds 105 dB. Suggest a warning system: first exceedance results in a verbal warning, second in a written warning, and third in a reduction of volume for the rest of the set.
Remarks: Monitoring frequency added in v0.4. Warning system added in v0.4.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ENTRY FY2025-052
Date: 14 Jun 2025
Reviewer: Marcus Tan [MT]
Policy ID: PD-ACC-01-2025 (Accessibility & Inclusion)
Version under review: v0.1
Comment:
Section 2 on accessible facilities says "all public areas shall be accessible to persons with disabilities." This is a good general statement, but the draft lacks specifics. Suggest adding requirements for accessible toilets (at least one per zone), accessible viewing platforms at the main stage, and clear signage for accessible routes. Also, the draft does not mention how we will handle requests for additional accommodations, such as sign language interpretation for the announcement stage.
